headline: Southborough prepared for Special Town Meeting while school planners focused on a $38 million Neary School renovation and committees reviewed FY28 fiscal pressures.
synopsis: In October 2026, town boards focused heavily on final preparations and warrant recommendations for the October 17 Special Town Meeting. The Elementary School Building Committee shifted focus to an estimated $38 million addition-renovation plan for Neary Elementary after architects determined a $15 million baseline upgrade would trigger extensive mandatory code work without addressing major mechanical needs. Ahead of Special Town Meeting, the Advisory Committee recommended spending $240,000 from water reserves to connect two homes near the Parkerville landfill, while the Select Board declined to retain $100,000 in unissued debt for Breakneck Hill restoration. The Community Preservation Committee and Trails Committee opted to bring forward the $217,318 Peninsula Trail bridge article as written despite prior negative advisory votes. In school operations, the School Committee approved a contract amendment aligning Southborough teacher pay scales with Algonquin Regional High School, and regional subcommittees began planning for FY28 budget constraints.

top_items.title: Neary School Building Project Focuses on $38 Million Plan
top_items.why: Architects revealed that a baseline $15 million repair scope would leave only $5.8 million for direct work after code-mandated upgrades. Planners shifted focus to an estimated $38 million addition and renovation plan.
top_items.body: Tappé Architects presented a cost breakdown showing that a $15 million upgrade to Margaret A. Neary Elementary School would be consumed largely by soft costs, contingencies, and mandatory ADA and fire sprinkler code triggers. Because it would not address replacing aging univents, boilers, or educational spaces, the Elementary School Building Committee decided to advance schematic design for the $38 million addition and renovation option ahead of a planned March 2027 Town Meeting vote.

top_items.title: Peninsula Trail Bridge Warrant Article Advanced Without Cuts
top_items.why: The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to keep the $217,318 CPA request on the Special Town Meeting warrant as printed. The Trails Committee dropped plans for a floor amendment to reduce funding.
top_items.body: Facing negative recommendations from both the Select Board and Advisory Committee over cost and operating budget pressures, the Trails Committee and Community Preservation Committee considered scaling back the $428,550 pedestrian footbridge project. After debate, the CPC voted 3-2 to bring the article to the floor as written, and the Trails Committee finalized an informational FAQ for voters focusing on pedestrian safety along Route 30.

top_items.title: School Committee Aligns Teacher Salaries with Algonquin Scale
top_items.why: The School Committee voted 5-0 to approve contract amendments with the Southborough Teachers Association Unit A. The agreement aligns local teacher salaries with Algonquin Regional High School starting July 1, 2027.
top_items.body: Following executive session discussions, the Southborough School Committee unanimously approved contract changes covering Articles 22 and 29 of the Unit A collective bargaining agreement. The amendments restructure the retirement incentive program and align Southborough's teacher pay schedule with that of Algonquin Regional High School, with adjustments scheduled to take effect for the 2027-2028 school year.

top_items.title: Advisory Committee Recommends Water Line to Parkerville Landfill Abutters
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee voted 6-0 to recommend Article 7, appropriating $240,000 from water retained earnings. The town will fund the entire connection cost into two private homes.
top_items.body: The Advisory Committee endorsed Article 7 for the Special Town Meeting after confirming that the town would cover full connection expenses from the street to the houses for two properties near the capped Parkerville Road landfill. The project extends the town water main to eliminate health risks and state-mandated private well monitoring after chemicals were detected in nearby monitoring wells.

top_items.title: Select Board Opposes Retaining Unissued Breakneck Hill Debt
top_items.why: The Select Board voted unanimously against offering or supporting a floor amendment to retain $100,000 in unissued borrowing authority for Breakneck Hill. Article 6 will move forward to rescind the full authorization.
top_items.body: The Conservation Commission and Stewardship Committee had requested preserving $100,000 in unissued borrowing authority from the completed Breakneck Hill Farm dump remediation to fund ongoing site restoration. The Select Board declined to support any change to Article 6, arguing that the full $727,960 in unused debt authorizations should be rescinded and pointing out that $176,000 in previously borrowed funds remains available.

top_items.title: Regional School Subcommittees Review FY28 Pressures and Healthcare Savings
top_items.why: School leadership warned of tight municipal budgets under Proposition 2 1/2 and proposed restructuring employee health insurance deductibles. The change could save an estimated $600,000 across the region.
top_items.body: The Regional School Committee's budget and capital subcommittees reviewed five FY28 capital requests totaling approximately $460,000 for Algonquin Regional High School. Administrators noted that while debt from the 2004 renovation will retire at the end of FY27—reducing regional debt service by roughly $800,000—operating budget pressures will require modeling level-service, 3% capped, and level-funded scenarios.

top_items.title: State Enacts Special Legislation for Costco Alcohol License
top_items.why: Special legislation signed by the governor grants Southborough authority to issue an additional off-premises liquor license for Costco.
top_items.body: Southborough's town administrator announced that the governor enacted special legislation authorizing an additional off-premises alcohol license specifically for Costco, giving the town until October 4, 2028, to formally grant the license. The announcement came alongside receipt of over $1.3 million in state and federal grants, including $1.1 million from MassWorks for Southville Road.
